course_title: Human Development and Relationships Across the Life Span
course_description:
This course is designed to prepare you for clinical practice, and to develop therapeutic skills in your field of study. The course explores mental health treatment in the context of human development, relationships and culture. You will critically analyse, evaluate and develop your knowledge and skills in these areas. You will also be required to develop a critique of your own development, and how this informs your sensitivity in working with clients at different stages of development. The focus is on the integration of theory and practice and the application of generalist and specialist skills within a human developmental, relational and cultural context.

This foundational course lays a strong groundwork for further study and professional practice in mental health, psychotherapy, and art therapy. Central to any mental health encounter is understanding a person’s development, relationships, cultural experience, and identity. Equally important is being attuned to our own sense of self to provide ethical, client-focused care.

Throughout this course, we will explore human life across all developmental stages, examining how culture, identity, and relationships influence who we are, how we view the world, and how we experience mental health concerns. The course emphasises a multicultural, trauma-informed, and social model approach to care, affirming consumer perspectives within the mental health system.

Tutorials are held weekly (except for week 3) via Zoom, and begin in Week 1. Set readings, videos and multimedia content accompany each tutorial topic to broaden and deepen reflective thinking into areas of human development and identity. This content is required to have been read/viewed prior to the group tutorial, to inspire rich discussion of the weeks focus topic. You are encouraged to discuss real life applications of learning and where possible offer experiential examples in class to fellow students.

We look forward to working with you and supporting your journey in this vital field.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with knowledge and experience that will encourage person focused, culturally sensitive and effective mental health practice and enable students to deliver quality mental health care with people across the lifespan.

learning_outcomes.description: Identify, understand and apply critical analysis to selected key theories of human development as they apply to the field of study
Demonstrate specialist skills and knowledge required to work with clients mental health challenges throughout the lifespan.
Understand the importance of human relationships and the broader socio-cultural environment, and how they can either enhance or impact negatively on mental health.
Understand the importance of developing cultural perspectives and learning to apply cultural sensitivity and humility when working with clients.

assessment_details.task_description: Each student will have the opportunity to lead their class in a 10-minute activity or therapeutic directive that is relevant to the weekly topic. This will be followed by a 5-minute Q&A relating to your activity. This assessment does not require you to summarise the weeks topic/learning resources. This is an opportunity to practice the application of therapeutic skills with your peers, and to demonstrate authentic engagement with the week’s topic, readings and learning resources. Examples of an activity or therapeutic directive could include; facilitating a therapeutic intervention that might be used in practice with a client or consumer from a particular demographic leading a reflective exercise based on one of the weeks learning resources designing an activity or directive which applies learning from the readings into practice Examples of questions you could be asked relating to your activity could include (but are not limited to); How did the learning materials provided this week influence the tutorial activity you have chosen? What was your clinical reasoning behind choosing the activity/directive you facilitated this week? Is there anything you might do differently if you had the opportunity to facilitate this activity again? Please note, as this is an oral assessment, the Leading Tutorial Activity component of the tutorial will be recorded. The activity will be marked against a rubric that will be available to students. Criteria and Marking Choose, design or adapt an activity or therapeutic directive which is relevant to the weekly topic - 5% Facilitate an activity or therapeutic directive, including integrating the intended learning as it relates to the weekly topic - 10% Respond to questions relating to the chosen activity, including both planning and facilitation, demonstrating authentic authorship and engagement with the assessment process - 15% Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Family Experiences and Therapeutic Practice
assessment_details.task_description: Part One: Family Genogram/Community Map Create a genogram and/or a map of your family or chosen community, to reflect on key relationships and family experiences. This visual representation should include relevant key relationships and, where possible, encompass two to three generations members. Use standard symbols and elements of a genogram, or an alternative mapping method, to illustrate the structure and connections within your family/community. Part Two: Reflective Essay In a 1400-word essay, reflect on how your family of origin, family experiences, and key relationships have shaped your identity and worldview – who you are and how you see the world. Articulate key themes, challenges, and learnings that have influenced your life and professional practice in mental health. Address the following points in your reflection: Influence on Therapeutic Practice Discuss how your family, cultural, and community experiences and relationships have shaped your childhood, development, and worldview. Explain how these experiences influence your therapeutic practice with individuals and families. Connection to Self Articulate the connection between your experiences and your current sense of self and way of being. State the boundaries of confidentiality and safety you used when deciding what information to include in your essay. Impact on Professional Values Reflect on how your family, culture, community, and relationships have impacted your professional values and practice in mental health. Present both the strengths and challenges that your experiences bring to your therapeutic practice and alliance. Your essay should be self-reflective and well-written, adhering to the word limit. No references are required. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric that will be available for students. Criteria and Marking 1. Student presents a Genogram/Map of their family (to the best of the student's knowledge) including relevant key relationships and where possible two to three generations of family members. Genogram must make use of standard symbols and elements of a genogram, or an alternative map, of the family/community structure showing the relationship between multiple people and the student. 2. Student demonstrates reflection on their family experiences, cultural and community experiences and relationships as presented in the genogram, including how these have shaped the student's childhood, development, relationships and worldview. The student is able to articulate the connection between their experiences and their current sense of self and way of being. The student is able to state the boundaries of confidentiality used when making decisions about what information to reflect upon in this essay. 3. Student is able to demonstrate reflection how their experience of family, culture, community, family experiences and relationships have influenced or impacted their professional values and practice in mental health. The student is able to present both strengths and challenges that their experiences offer to their therapeutic practice and therapeutic alliance. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Mental Health Challenges Across the Lifespan
assessment_details.task_description: Part One: Therapeutic Resource Select a developmental period and target population discussed in the course, and create a therapeutic resource addressing a mental health challenge experienced by this population. Possible formats include a pamphlet, fact sheet, video, animation, podcast, poster, or worksheets. The resource should provide both psychoeducation and therapeutic strategies suitable for consumers or carers during mental health support. Part Two: Written Guide Accompany your therapeutic resource with a written guide (maximum 1000 words) intended for other therapists/health professionals. This guide should assist them in using the resource with their consumers/carers. Submission Instructions Compile both your resource and written guide into one file for submission via Turnitin. For audio/video files, save the file in your University One Drive folder or a similar electronic drive and include a link in your submitted PDF/Word document. Criteria and Marking: Therapeutic Resource 1. Create a therapeutic resource tailored to one developmental stage in human development, providing a definition and contemporary perspective of the developmental stage chosen in the context of mental health and wellbeing. A target population and mental health challenge within the developmental stage is identified. The intended audience/recipient of the resource and the goals/objectives of the resource are clear. 2. The resource focuses on one mental health challenge relevant to the target population and explains the key components and/or implications on mental health and wellbeing, including the bio-psycho-social, cultural, relational and developmental factors, and references the contemporary understandings of this issue in Australian society. 3. The therapeutic resource provides learning and strategies relevant and appropriate to the target population to support and improve their wellbeing in the context of the mental health challenge discussed. The resource must provide a minimum of 2 relevant activities or therapeutic processes and detail the practical steps of the activities for the person to use in their daily life, including and any limitations or caveats. Written Guide 4. A written guide (maximum 1000 words) accompanies the therapeutic resource, intended for therapists and other health professionals to assist in the use of this resource with their consumers/carers. The guide details the context and purpose of the resource, the key concepts and theories of development utilized, the evidence for the activities/therapeutic processes shared and the potential usage in practice. Format, Presentation and Writing 5. When read or spoken or watched, the content is a minimum length of 4 minutes and is no longer than 5 minutes. Resource is presented in a consumer-friendly format appropriate for the intended audience. The resource uses appropriate in text/spoken referencing of literature/theories where relevant (references not required). The written guide is not more than 1000 words, and is written appropriately for other therapists and health professionals. Referenced according to APA7 guidelines, and includes a reference list. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric that will be available for students. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Week 1 - Culture Humility and Self in the Therapeutic Alliance Culture Humility and Self in the Therapeutic Alliance Introduction to PXMH7104, Culture Humility and Self in the Therapeutic Alliance. Preparation for Workshops in Week 3. Why is understanding human development and relationships important for therapists and mental health practitioners? In what ways is it important that we understand our own experience and culture as we work in therapy and mental health? How do we negotiate the connection and alliance between the person and our own human self? How does culture and our upbringing influence our work with others? How do we manage difference? How do we see the world and how this influences our interaction in the world? Learning outcomes: L03, L04

Week 2 - Identity, Gender, Sexuality and Belonging Identity, Gender, Sexuality and Belonging How does my assigned gender and experienced gender differ or match? How do norms or perceptions impact my mental health and sense of self? How does my personal identity interact or fit with those of my family, community and society at large? What does belonging mean and what happens when I don’t belong? How does my identity (or discrimination for my identity) impact my mental health, and in what contexts and why? How much do I know about the needs of LGBTIQA+ people and who I can support them as a therapist? Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

Week 3 - Workshops - Residential Week In week 3 of Semester you will attend several on campus group workshops, including: Cultural Humility in Practice - Tuesday 11th August 8:30-12pm Identity and Inclusive Mental Health Practice - Tuesday 11th August 1-4:30pm Child and Adolescent Art Therapy - Thursday 13th August 8:30-12pm These in person workshops are part of a week long residential suite of workshops, and are compulsory for all students in PXMH7104. Preparation - Please watch the Cultural Humility video (approx. 1 hr) and Child Art Therapy presentation delivered by the UQ team prior to attending the workshops. Please also prepare for participation in the morning workshop - details will be provided to you via email and in your tutorials. If you have any concerns contact Course Coordinator Dani Walsh to discuss further. Please note attendance hours in this course are a requirement for future registration and accreditation with peak bodies. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Family and Relationship Structures Family and Relationship Structures How much do I know and understand about my own family and its impact on me and my work? How are other families organised? How does family structure/organisation impact on their strengths and vulnerabilities? Consider the experience of being taken away from your family - how might this impact mental health? And relationships? What key skills and perspectives are required when working with the complexity of family and family/community structures in mental health? Learning outcomes: L01, L03

Infancy, Attachment, Parenting Infancy, Attachment and Parenting How does our experience of early relationships with our caregivers influence our development, our sense of self, our world view, our interpersonal skills and sensitivities? How does attachment and early relationships impact children, and impact humans in later life? How do we view development within the infant (and even pre -birth) and the link with relationships and attachment? What is the experience of transitioning to parenthood, in relation to mental health, relationships, identity, and wellbeing? How does culture influence our thinking about these life stages/transitions? Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Early Childhood Early Childhood Consider the balance between learning, autonomy and the need for closeness through this developmental period - how can these needs coexist? How do developmental issues start to arise and be experienced by the child, and identified by surrounding adults? How does the experience of trauma or significant change impact development? What are A.C.E.’s and how do they manifest in childhood and throughout life? How do we support young children in this period? What mental health strengths and needs or concerns arise at this stage? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Middle Childhood Middle Childhood This is the time where (most) children are going to school, making friends, learning and exploring the world, learning about who they are and what they like, taking on new responsibilities. What does wellness and mental health look like through this life stage? What key changes and identity shifts are occurring in this developmental period? What challenges might arise? What do relationships look like at this point in life? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Adolescence Adolescence How does identity shift in this period of life? Intra-personally, interpersonally, within family and social groups and in the broader context of the world? In what ways do social media platforms and digital peer groups impact identity formation due this life stage? How does society view this demographic? What messages are prevalent in the media? How might culture influence thinking/perception about this life stage? What is the key to wellness and positive mental health for this demographic? How do we manage the risks of mental health, self harm and suicidality that arise? How do we support young people, families and the wider community? How do we engage a recovery model when an adolescent in is tension between being cared for and being independent? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Early Adulthood to Adulthood Early Adulthood to Adulthood How does our society see this period of life? What is important? What is expected? What are the key stressors? What was your experience of transitioning to the adult world and to adult responsibilities? How might culture influence behaviour and expectations for this demographic? How to relationships change through this period of life? What mental health and wellbeing issues might this demographic be vulnerable to? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Middle to Mature Adulthood Middle to Mature Adulthood What does mental health look like through different parts of adulthood? Consider the impact of changes and transitions of relationships, career, life goals, looking both forward and back - what is unique about this stage of life? How might relationships and family structure change for this demographic? How can strengths, needs, hopes and goals sustain or change or evolve over time? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Old Age Old Age This period of life comes with many transitions. What might some of these be, and how might they impact mental health and wellbeing? How does identity and culture influence perspectives for this demographic? What does wellness look like in this life stage? What mental health concerns become relevant at this time? What are the benefits of being older and having lived and experienced a lifetime of relationships and circumstances? What are some of the challenges? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

End of Life End of Life End of life can occur when you are in old age, or much earlier due to illness or other concerns. How does being near the end of our life impact our sense of self, the world and mental health and wellness. How can therapists support individuals, families and communities in situations of palliative care, life limited conditions, enduring suicidality, grief and loss? What does life and death mean in my culture? How does my family engage in or understand end of life and beyond? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Emotional and Social Development Emotional and Social Development How do I prefer to “be” in society? In my community? How do I prefer to interact with others? What challenges do I face in social settings and why? Am I an introvert, extrovert, a social butterfly, a quiet achiever, an observer? What do these terms mean anyway? Are they important? How do I perceive care, love, support from others? How does this impact my coping, my perception of mental health, my expression of resiliency, my sense of self? Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
